category: exchange rate API (central bank reference rates, daily, history to 1948)

free_tier.stated: Free public API at api.frankfurter.dev: no key, no quotas, no monthly or daily caps; requests are rate-limited only to prevent abuse; 228 currencies from 106 central banks and official sources, history back to 1948
free_tier.notes: v2 is current and v1 is deprecated but stays available. Rates update once a day. Output is JSON, CSV or NDJSON. Keyless v1 and v2 rate calls answered HTTP 200; one earlier call answered a transient 522.

per_object_cap.stated: not stated; narrow quotes and use NDJSON for large date ranges

egress.terms: not metered; no quota is stated

interface_detail: GET https://api.frankfurter.dev/v2/rates, /v2/rate/BASE/QUOTE and /v2/providers/ecb/rates; .csv suffix or Accept: application/x-ndjson for CSV and NDJSON; an MCP server at mcp.frankfurter.dev
tooling: curl or any HTTP client; the open-source project can also be installed and run by the user with Docker, which is the last resort after the hosted public API.
chaining: Keyless daily reference rates to convert prices from the crypto and finance records; cache the daily rows locally.

limits.value: rate-limited to prevent abuse, size not published; no monthly or daily caps

limits_note: Bulk path: request a date range with from and to as NDJSON or CSV to stream the whole series. Storage terms: storing daily observations locally for caching or analytics is encouraged by the vendor.
binding_note: Only an unpublished abuse limit exists; there is no quota.

identity_cost.detail: No key and no account: the vendor says no API key is needed and keyless calls answered HTTP 200.

reliability_note: One call answered a transient HTTP 522 from the edge; later calls answered 200.
confidence_note: Terms are read from the vendor page; keyless v1 and v2 calls answered 200; the abuse limit was not measured.

evidence.proved: 228 currencies from 106 sources, daily, back to 1948
evidence.quote: Frankfurter is a free exchange rates API for 228 currencies from 106 central banks and official sources. Rates update daily and go back to 1948.
You don't need an API key.

evidence.proved: no quotas or monthly or daily caps
evidence.quote: There are no quotas. Requests are rate-limited to prevent abuse, but there are no monthly or daily caps.

evidence.proved: storing daily observations locally is encouraged
evidence.quote: Storing daily observations locally for caching or historical analytics is encouraged to keep API traffic light.
Each line is one independent JSON object, useful for streaming large time series without buffering the entire response.

evidence.proved: a keyless v2 rates call answered HTTP 200

notes: Keyless, no quotas. Bulk path: date ranges as NDJSON or CSV. Storage: local caching is encouraged.
